subject: Service account taxonomy & SSO/SCIM org-policy alignment
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@financia.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@financia.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service account taxonomy & SSO/SCIM org-policy alignment

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we lock the implementation cadence, we want to align on two items that often create friction during cutover: service-account naming + roles mapping, and org-level policies that affect SCIM provisioning (e.g., excluded groups, protected attributes, and IP allowlist expectations).

Goals for this thread:
- Propose a simple service-account naming taxonomy that works across your environments (staging/prod) and across Redwood’s service-account patterns.
- Confirm SCIM attribute mapping for our initial provisioning wave (users + groups + service accounts).
- Agree any org policies or IP allowlist rules we must respect for API calls from Redwood during the rollout window.

Attachments: I’m attaching a working spreadsheet (service-account-naming-v1.xlsx) and a YAML sample for SCIM attribute mapping (scim-attribute-mapping.yaml).

Questions for you:
1) Do you require runtime IP allowlist entries for Redwood’s SCIM API endpoints, or is per-request validation (mutual TLS + token) sufficient for initial provisioning?
2) Are there protected attributes we must never overwrite via SCIM (e.g., employee_type, cost_center)? If so, please list them and whether they are writable by HR or only by admin.
3) Naming: would "svc-redwood-{env}-{purpose}-{shortid}" (example: svc-redwood-prod-ingest-01) work for you, or do you need a different delimiter/ordering to fit your audit scripts?

Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize taxonomy and capture any org-policy exceptions. Suggested slots: 10:00am or 2:30pm PT.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0128

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for LLMs
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@financia.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@financia.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service account taxonomy & SSO/SCIM org-policy alignment

Monica —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:
- We prefer IP allowlist for the production SCIM calls; staging can be done without it. We’ll provide the CIDR blocks once we lock the rollout date.
- Protected attributes: cost_center and employee_type must be read-only via SCIM. Job_title and manager are writable.
- Naming: the suggested pattern looks fine, but we need a prefix that ties the account to the owning team for audit queries (e.g., svc-redwood-{team}-{env}-{purpose}-{id}). We’ll share a short list of team codes.

I can do 2:30pm PT tomorrow. Tom will join for the IP/Palo Alto firewall constraints.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Security Operations — Financia
elena.ruiz@financia.com | +1 212-555-9876

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service account taxonomy & SSO/SCIM org-policy alignment

Folks —

Quick internal notes ahead of the sync:
- Naming taxonomy: prefer ordering that makes automated parsing deterministic. My recommendation: svc-redwood-{teamcode}.{env}.{purpose}.{shortid} (dots are easier for our log-parsers). Example: svc-redwood.cardsvc.prod.ingest.01
- Service account roles: keep to least privilege for initial wave; create a separate 'provisioner' role that only calls SCIM/Groups scopes. Avoid attaching admin-level scopes at creation.
- SCIM mapping: we should NOT map cost_center or employee_type as Elena noted; mark them as read-only in the YAML and add a pre-provision validation step that rejects writes to protected attributes with a descriptive error for the API.
- IP allowlist: when Financia provides CIDRs, we can lock production endpoints and add staging exceptions. We should also record the firewall ticket (Tom) to avoid mid-cutover drops.

I attached a short worksheet in the Drive link Monica included with the proposed column mapping and a validation checklist.

Action items I want on the call:
1) Finalize teamcode list (Elena to provide)
2) Agree on shortid length (2 vs 3 digits) — for now use 2 digits as default
3) Confirm rollout order for groups vs users vs service accounts (we usually provision service accounts last)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Recap & next steps: 

Recap (decisions):
- Naming: svc-redwood.{teamcode}.{env}.{purpose}.{shortid} (example: svc-redwood.cardsvc.prod.ingest.01). Elena will send the teamcode list today.
- Protected SCIM attributes: cost_center, employee_type = read-only. Job_title and manager writable. Redwood will set server-side checks to reject write attempts to protected attributes.
- IP allowlist: Financia to provide production CIDRs. Redwood will restrict production SCIM endpoints to those CIDRs on go‑live; staging will remain open to allow initial validation.
- Provisioning order: users -> groups -> service accounts (service accounts created last).

Action items:
- Elena: share teamcode list + production CIDR blocks (by EOD Monday).
- Tom: open firewall change ticket and share tracking ID (JIRA/CHG number) before cutover.
- Ben/Karthik: finalize YAML mapping (mark protected attributes read-only) and add validation error codes. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d-financia-onboard
- Monica: schedule the 30-min follow-up (2:30pm PT tomorrow confirmed).

Attachments referenced: service-account-naming-v1.xlsx, scim-attribute-mapping.yaml (uploaded to the Drive folder).

If there are any blockers before the call, flag them in this thread so we can escalate to the Infra on-call.

Best —
